messages:
micah: Quick sync — post-launch backlog question. We keep getting asks that feel like 'ownership bias' (team asks are higher priority because someone raised their hand). We need a lightweight rule to decide patch vs next minor. Proposal: short rubric + 48h triage owner + fastpatch window. Thoughts?

anya: +1 to rubric. Can we fold in "customer SLA impact" as the tiebreaker? Some asks are noisy but not customer-facing. :thinking_face:

tara: Agree on owner. Suggest rotating 48h owner from oncall/product so we don't stall. Also: define what counts as "fastpatch" (critical bugfix only?).

liam: My 2c: fastpatch = regressions and security + top-N customer blocking. Everything else goes to next minor. Keeps scope small.

micah: Nice. Draft rubber-stamp rubric (very short) — open to editing:```
triage rubric v0.1
- severity: Sev1 (production outage) / Sev2 (customer-blocking) / Sev3 (QOL)
- customers_affected: >5 = high / 1-5 = medium / 0 (internal) = low
- reproducible: yes/no
- workaround: none/fragile/ok
- recommended_action: fastpatch if (Sev1 or Sev2 and customers_affected=high) OR security/regression
```

jenna: Love it. Can we add a line for "cost to fix (dev days)" as a sanity check? If fix is 10 dev days and impact is medium, maybe schedule instead.

micah: Good call. Add it. Also propose we publish a one-pager in the handbook and a quick Slack command for triage owners to tag. Eg `/fastpatch request <ticket>` that 48h-owner acknowledges.

anya: For the handbook snippet, can we include acceptance criteria for the fastpatch rollout? i.e., automatic rollback plan, QA smoke steps, and canary % (10% -> 100% over 30m). Keeps releases safe.

liam: We'll need SRE alignment on rollback/canary defaults. @sre-bot any preference?

sre-bot: Deploy policy reminder: canary rollout recommended for all fastpatches unless rollback impossible. Default: 10% for 15m, 50% for 15m, 100% if healthy. See runbook: https://internal/runbooks/rollouts

tara: OK — decision path looks like: 1) reporter files ticket, 2) 48h owner triages against rubric, 3) if fastpatch -> open patch branch + small PR + SRE rollout + communicate to impacted customers. 4) if not fastpatch -> schedule in next minor with PM owner.

micah: I'll draft the handbook blurb and the `/fastpatch` slash template this afternoon. Can someone own the 48h rota for the next two weeks?

anya: I can take the rota this week.

jenna: I'm up for next week.

liam: I'll draft the handbook blurb and add the cost-to-fix field to the rubric.

micah: Awesome. Action items: micah -> handbook draft + slash command template; liam -> update rubric in GH issue #4521; anya -> 48h owner this week; jenna -> 48h next week; tara -> sync with SRE on canary/runbook if anything needs changing.

jenna: Quick note — for customer-facing bugs tagged as P2, please @sales when we triage so account teams know potential impact. Helps with comms. :+1:

micah: Agreed — add notification step to the template. I'll ping legal if any data/privacy edge cases crop up.

liam: Cool. If no objections I'll post the GH issue with rubric + blurb draft by EOD.

anya: No objections from me. :rocket:

sre-bot: Deploy bot: new canary policy acknowledged by SRE team.
